biological.citation: A brain-to-gut signal controls intestinal fat absorption (PMID: 39261733)
biological.summary: GABRA1 (the α1 subunit of GABAA receptor) is expressed in dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV) neurons and mediates the effect of puerarin on intestinal fat absorption. Conditional Gabra1 knockout in the DMV largely abolished puerarin-induced intestinal fat loss. Cryogenic electron microscopy revealed puerarin binds to an allosteric modulatory site on the GABAA receptor containing GABRA1.

biological.citation: An airway-to-brain sensory pathway mediates influenza-induced sickness (PMID: 36890237)
biological.summary: GABRA1 is expressed in a specific subpopulation of glossopharyngeal sensory neurons (petrosal GABRA1 neurons) that detect PGE2 and mediate influenza-induced sickness behavior in mice. Ablation of petrosal GABRA1 neurons or targeted knockout of the PGE2 receptor EP3 in these neurons eliminated influenza-induced decreases in food intake, water intake, and mobility. These neurons project to mucosal regions of the nasopharynx and display specific axonal targeting in the brainstem.

biological.citation: GABRA1-Related Disorders: From Genetic to Functional Pathways (PMID: 37606373)
biological.summary: Functional analysis of 19 GABRA1 variants in 27 individuals revealed that variants in the extracellular domain and small transmembrane loops cause loss-of-function (LoF) effects associated with mild cognitive impairment and infantile-onset epilepsy, while variants in pore-forming transmembrane helices cause either gain-of-function (GoF) or LoF effects with more severe phenotypes including early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. GoF variants were specifically associated with severe early-onset neurodevelopmental disorders, establishing a genotype-phenotype correlation framework for GABRA1-related disorders.

biological.citation: Characterization of the zebrafish gabra1(sa43718/sa43718) germline loss of function allele confirms a function for Gabra1 in motility and nervous system development (PMID: 38908344)
biological.summary: A zebrafish nonsense germline mutant allele (sa43718) of gabra1 causes decreased gabra1 mRNA expression associated with light-induced hypermotility (seizure-like behavior). Loss of gabra1 was accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of gabra2, gabra3, and gabra5, and proteomics analysis revealed abnormal expression of proteins regulating synaptic vesicle fusion, vesicle transport, synapse development, and mitochondrial protein complexes.

biological.citation: Understanding paralogous epilepsy-associated GABA(A) receptor variants (PMID: 39642202)
biological.summary: Electrophysiological analysis of the GABRA1 variant α1P260L and α1P260S in α1β2/3γ2 receptors demonstrated gain-of-function effects by increasing GABA sensitivity 3- to 23-fold, sometimes accompanied by loss-of-function traits such as reduced maximal current amplitude and enhanced receptor desensitization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed similar structural changes from all M1 proline mutations but with position-dependent asymmetry, establishing that paralogous variants at the conserved M1 proline residue all lead to overall GOF traits.

biological.citation: Epilepsy plus blindness in microdeletion of GABRA1 and GABRG2 in mouse and human (PMID: 37703949)
biological.summary: Haploinsufficiency of both GABRA1 and GABRG2 in mice (Gabra1+/-/Gabrg2+/- model) caused spontaneous seizures, reduced GABAA receptor α1, β2, and γ2 subunit expression in multiple brain regions, reduced electroretinography oscillatory potential, and optic nerve degeneration with impaired axonal myelination. This mouse model recapitulated the human patient phenotype of intractable epilepsy and blindness due to optic atrophy, and phenobarbital was identified as the most effective anticonvulsant in both mouse and patient.

biological.citation: Mir-139-5p inhibits glioma cell proliferation and progression by targeting GABRA1 (PMID: 34001135)
biological.summary: GABRA1 was identified as a functional downstream target of miR-139-5p in glioma cells; miR-139-5p overexpression inhibited glioma cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro, while upregulation of GABRA1 effectively reversed these inhibitory effects. Low miR-139-5p expression correlated with worse survival probability and higher WHO grade in glioma patients, establishing a miR-139-5p/GABRA1 regulatory axis in glioma progression.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Whole exome sequencing in epilepsy reveals significant gene burden of ultra-rare deleterious variants (ASHG 2018 - Feng et al.)
biological.summary: In the Epi25 Consortium WES study of 4,443 patients with genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE), GABRA1 showed significant enrichment of ultra-rare deleterious variants compared to 17,668 controls (OR=21.5, p=3×10⁻⁴), making it one of the strongest gene associations for GGE. This large-scale burden analysis confirms GABRA1 as a major risk gene for common generalized epilepsy.

biological.citation: Impaired GABAergic regulation and developmental immaturity in interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence in the tuberous sclerosis complex (PMID: 38714540)
biological.summary: Single-nuclei RNA sequencing of TSC patient brain tissue revealed downregulation of GABRA1 specifically in somatostatin-expressing (SST+) interneurons, accompanied by upregulation of GABRA2, indicating a subunit composition shift associated with developmental immaturity. This altered GABRA1 expression in SST+ interneurons was linked to disrupted maturation and incomplete switch from excitatory to inhibitory GABAergic signaling in TSC.

biological.citation: Differential Expression of GABA Receptor-Related Genes in Alzheimer's Disease (PMID: 39752101)
biological.summary: GABRA1 mRNA expression was significantly decreased in the hippocampus of AD model mice (D-galactose-induced), and aerobic exercise increased hippocampal GABRA1 and GABRG2 expression while reducing astrocyte neurotoxicity markers (TNF-α, IL-1β, GFAP). Bioinformatic analysis of human AD datasets (GSE36980, GSE48350) identified GABRA1 as one of four core downregulated hub genes with good diagnostic value (ROC analysis) in AD hippocampus.
